name: Assortion
summary: Shopify app for upsells, cross-sells, product add-ons and cart customization, with one feature set on every plan and a price set by the store's total monthly orders.
best_for: Shopify stores that want upsells, cross-sells, product add-ons and cart customization in one app at a flat price that grows with order volume rather than as a share of upsell revenue
skip_if: your store has many orders but low margins, since the price rises with every order whether or not an upsell sells; or you want upsell blocks outside the product page
honest_knock: The price follows your total store orders, so you pay the same whether the upsells sell or not, and busy months can push you into the next tier. App blocks only work on product pages. We found no refund or cancellation policy, and the page does not say how refunded orders or a tier change mid-month are handled.

pricing.entry_price_terms: 0-50 orders · per month, set by total monthly store orders, not only orders with an upsell
pricing.notes: (read 2026-10-15 on assortion.com/pricing and the Shopify App Store listing apps.shopify.com/assortion, prices in USD) Assortion has one feature set and charges by the size of your store: the price depends on your total monthly store orders, not only the orders that include an upsell. 0 to 50 orders a month costs $9.99, 51 to 200 costs $19.99, 201 to 500 costs $34.99, 501 to 1,000 costs $59.99, 1,001 to 2,500 costs $89.99, 2,501 to 5,000 costs $149.99 and more than 5,000 costs $199.99. The two top tiers overlap at exactly 5,000 orders on the page. The Shopify listing shows only the first three tiers and bills every 30 days. Development stores use the app for free with all features. Paid plans list a 14-day free trial, cart customization, upsells, product add-ons and live support. No annual price is shown. Re-read on 13 November 2026 with a plain fetch of assortion.com/pricing and the Shopify listing: all seven order tiers, the 14-day trial and free use on development stores are unchanged; the listing still bills in USD every 30 days.

schema_offer.description: 0-50 orders, per month, set by total monthly store orders, not only orders with an upsell; 51-200 orders $19.99, 201-500 $34.99, 501-1000 $59.99, 1001-2500 $89.99, 2501-5000 $149.99, 5000+ $199.99; free on development stores; 14-day trial; billed every 30 days through Shopify; no annual price shown. Read on the vendor's own pricing page on 2026-11-13.

compare_with.name: Selleasy
compare_with.why: Selleasy is in our dossiers too and solves the same problem with a different meter: when we read it on 19 September 2026 it charged a share of the sales it helped make, 3% on direct sales, 1% on assisted sales and 5% on upsells and cross-sells, with no subscription. Assortion charges a fixed monthly price set by your total orders, from $9.99. If upsells drive a lot of revenue per order, a flat fee is easier to predict; if they sell little, a revenue share costs less.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Assortion on a Shopify development store: the install, the Flex test charge approved without a payment method, one Frequently Bought Together widget set up in about 2 minutes and seen in the preview inside the app, the Plan page with the cancel dialog (closed without cancelling) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was billed. Install: the listing was read as text (Free plan available. Free trial available.; Development, Free, Free for development stores, All features are included; paid plans 0-50 ORDERS $9.99 / month, 50-200 ORDERS $19.99 / month and 200-500 ORDERS $34.99 / month, each with a 14-day free trial; All charges are billed in USD). The install form was sent at about 14:23 in our own tab; Shopify showed the Install app dialog with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved. Right after the install Shopify showed an Approve subscription screen: You will not be billed for this test charge., plan Flex, This app bills you for usage charges, an app spending limit of a maximum of $200,00 USD per 30 days, and You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec. with the note that billing starts when you begin to use the app. An Add payment method row was shown but was not required and not filled in. Because the screen said it was a test charge and no card was needed, we approved it; no payment method was entered and nothing was billed. The dashboard then opened with Generated revenue $0.00, Orders with upsells 0, a notice that the App embed is off and a setup guide 0 / 2 completed (Create your first widget, Set up the cart drawer). No separate account, demo, call or phone number was asked. Core action, one Frequently Bought Together offer, about 2 minutes (14:23 to 14:25) and about 12 steps: Create widget, a choice of 12 types (Bundle Builder, Volume Discount, Frequently Bought Together, Product Add-ons, Popup Upsell, Popup Cross-sell, Post purchase offer, Product Recommendations, In-cart recommendation, Checkout Upsell, Free gift, Gift Wrap), Frequently Bought Together, the name Assortion test bundle, the trigger product The Collection Snowboard: Liquid, the offer products The Collection Snowboard: Hydrogen and Oxygen, Save. A toast said Widget created successfully, the page said Last updated today at 2:25 PM, the status was Active, and the preview inside the app showed Frequently Bought Together with three snowboards, Total Price: $2,374.95 and the button Add selected to Cart. Only the preview inside the app was seen. The theme preview and the theme editor were not opened, the app embed stayed Off, so the widget was not seen on a store page, and no theme change was saved. Plans: on a development store the app shows no plans and no order ladder, only the Flex plan with the spending limit of $200,00 USD per 30 days; the Plan page only shows Subscription and a Cancel subscription button. The order ladder of the listing and the dossier ($9.99 up to $199.99) was therefore not seen in the app. Cancelling: App, Plan, Cancel subscription opened the dialog Please confirm that you want to cancel your subscription with the buttons Cancel and Cancel subscription; we pressed Cancel, so the subscription was not cancelled. The app was uninstalled instead (Settings, Apps, the row of the app, Uninstall): the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason is required (we gave Testing multiple apps), and the app was gone from the installed apps afterwards. Not tested: the order ladder and tier changes, how refunds count, the widget in the store preview or theme editor, upsells beyond the product page, the checkout upsell, combining discounts and the thin margin case. Clean up: the widget Assortion test bundle stayed in the app and went away with the uninstall; no theme change was saved; other apps were not touched; our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The Approve subscription screen came directly after the install, the app shows no plans or order ladder on a development store, the app embed was off after the install, and the Plan page only has a cancel button.

claim_checks.claim: Shopify stores wanting upsells in one app
claim_checks.observed: The app offers 12 widget types in one place, among them Frequently Bought Together, Volume Discount, Popup Upsell and Checkout Upsell, and one Frequently Bought Together widget was set up in about 2 minutes and seen in the preview inside the app; the other types were not tried.
claim_checks.plan: Flex test charge approved, development store, nothing billed
claim_checks.comparability: Dossier one app wording versus the list of 12 widget types and one widget made; the other types were not tried.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: Several upsell types sit in one app and the first widget is quick to make; only one type was tried and only inside the app.

claim_checks.observed: No margin, refund or volume case was set up, so how the app behaves for a store with many orders and thin margins could not be checked; the app showed only a spending limit.
claim_checks.plan: Flex test charge approved, development store, nothing billed
claim_checks.comparability: Dossier thin margin wording versus a development store with no orders through the app.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The test says nothing about thin margins or high order volumes.

claim_checks.claim: Stores wanting upsells beyond the product page
claim_checks.observed: The Checkout Upsell and Post purchase offer types exist in the list, but only a Frequently Bought Together widget was made and it was not seen on a store page because the app embed stayed off.
claim_checks.plan: Flex test charge approved, development store, nothing billed
claim_checks.comparability: Dossier beyond the product page wording versus one widget seen only in the app preview.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The test says nothing about upsells beyond the product page.

claim_checks.claim: Free plan available. Free trial available.
claim_checks.observed: The listing says free plan available and the app opened without a payment method for the development store; the Approve screen said You will not be billed for this test charge. and a trial ending on 1 Dec.
claim_checks.plan: Flex test charge approved, development store, nothing billed
claim_checks.comparability: Dossier free on development stores versus the test charge screen on a development store.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: Free use on a development store matches the dossier; a normal store may be charged, which was not tested.

claim_checks.observed: The app shows no plans and no order ladder on a development store, only the Flex plan with a spending limit, so the prices of the listing ladder could not be compared with anything in the app.
claim_checks.plan: Flex test charge approved, development store, nothing billed
claim_checks.comparability: Dossier order ladder versus a Flex plan with a spending limit on a development store.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The order ladder from $9.99 a month was not shown in the app, so what a normal store pays could not be seen.

claim_checks.claim: You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec.
claim_checks.observed: The Shopify Approve screen says a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec. and that billing starts when the app is used, which matches the 14 days of the listing and the dossier; the screen also says the app bills usage charges.
claim_checks.plan: Flex test charge approved, development store, nothing billed
claim_checks.comparability: Dossier trial length versus the approval screen of 14 days.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: The trial length of 14 days matches the dossier, and usage charges follow after it.

claim_checks.observed: The Approve screen for Flex shows an app spending limit of a maximum of $200,00 USD per 30 days and no monthly price or tax line; the listing ladder of $9.99 to $199.99 was not shown, so no price could be set against the screen.
claim_checks.plan: Flex test charge approved, development store, nothing billed
claim_checks.comparability: Listing ladder prices versus a spending limit on the approval screen; no stored cost rule was compared.
claim_checks.buying_consequence: A spending limit of $200 per 30 days is not a price, and the amount a store pays depends on use.

exit_test.what: The app was installed on our Shopify development store, which we set up, and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 17 November 2026 the session tested Assortion on a Shopify development store: the install, the Flex test charge approved without a payment method, one Frequently Bought Together widget set up in about 2 minutes and seen in the preview inside the app, the Plan page with the cancel dialog (closed without cancelling) and the uninstall dialog, after which the app was uninstalled. Nothing was billed. Install: the listing was read as text (Free plan available. Free trial available.; Development, Free, Free for development stores, All features are included; paid plans 0-50 ORDERS $9.99 / month, 50-200 ORDERS $19.99 / month and 200-500 ORDERS $34.99 / month, each with a 14-day free trial; All charges are billed in USD). The install form was sent at about 14:23 in our own tab; Shopify showed the Install app dialog with View customer data, View staff and contributor data and View and edit store data, and the install was approved. Right after the install Shopify showed an Approve subscription screen: You will not be billed for this test charge., plan Flex, This app bills you for usage charges, an app spending limit of a maximum of $200,00 USD per 30 days, and You have a 14-day free trial ending on 1 Dec. with the note that billing starts when you begin to use the app. An Add payment method row was shown but was not required and not filled in. Because the screen said it was a test charge and no card was needed, we approved it; no payment method was entered and nothing was billed. The dashboard then opened with Generated revenue $0.00, Orders with upsells 0, a notice that the App embed is off and a setup guide 0 / 2 completed (Create your first widget, Set up the cart drawer). No separate account, demo, call or phone number was asked. Core action, one Frequently Bought Together offer, about 2 minutes (14:23 to 14:25) and about 12 steps: Create widget, a choice of 12 types (Bundle Builder, Volume Discount, Frequently Bought Together, Product Add-ons, Popup Upsell, Popup Cross-sell, Post purchase offer, Product Recommendations, In-cart recommendation, Checkout Upsell, Free gift, Gift Wrap), Frequently Bought Together, the name Assortion test bundle, the trigger product The Collection Snowboard: Liquid, the offer products The Collection Snowboard: Hydrogen and Oxygen, Save. A toast said Widget created successfully, the page said Last updated today at 2:25 PM, the status was Active, and the preview inside the app showed Frequently Bought Together with three snowboards, Total Price: $2,374.95 and the button Add selected to Cart. Only the preview inside the app was seen. The theme preview and the theme editor were not opened, the app embed stayed Off, so the widget was not seen on a store page, and no theme change was saved. Plans: on a development store the app shows no plans and no order ladder, only the Flex plan with the spending limit of $200,00 USD per 30 days; the Plan page only shows Subscription and a Cancel subscription button. The order ladder of the listing and the dossier ($9.99 up to $199.99) was therefore not seen in the app. Cancelling: App, Plan, Cancel subscription opened the dialog Please confirm that you want to cancel your subscription with the buttons Cancel and Cancel subscription; we pressed Cancel, so the subscription was not cancelled. The app was uninstalled instead (Settings, Apps, the row of the app, Uninstall): the dialog says you will no longer be able to use the app, that data managed by the app, such as discounts, will be deleted, and that a request goes to the app developer within 48 hours to delete all personal customer information; a reason is required (we gave Testing multiple apps), and the app was gone from the installed apps afterwards. Not tested: the order ladder and tier changes, how refunds count, the widget in the store preview or theme editor, upsells beyond the product page, the checkout upsell, combining discounts and the thin margin case. Clean up: the widget Assortion test bundle stayed in the app and went away with the uninstall; no theme change was saved; other apps were not touched; our own tabs were closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The Approve subscription screen came directly after the install, the app shows no plans or order ladder on a development store, the app embed was off after the install, and the Plan page only has a cancel button.
